questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I'm half French - and I have always dreamt about living in Paris.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The quality of my selected courses was not as good as I had expected - But Paris was magical and I found some really good friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very complicated, but thanks to the administration of UCPH I got the information that I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I only recieved some few "welcome-mails" with some practical information, thats all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived at "Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris" - It was super cool, they almost had everything (sport clubs, cantine, library, bank, etc.)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A cantine, a café and some restaurants.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's super cool - everyone is super sweet and helpfull - and it's probably a good way to start your student-life in Paris, if you are not used to the "french-way".

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very complicated - a lot of papers had to be signed and everything with the administration was super "old-school".

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: My host-university did not answer me for a long time, but after a while, I reached out to UCPH and they helped me to get through. Thank God!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: At my host-university? Almost nothing. But my professors were very nice to me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got what I wanted. But i only got the answer five days before take-off.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: "have ice in your stomach" (Danish expression), be super polite, and reach out to the administration of UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The quality of my selected courses, was not so good compared to UCPH. Everything worked out in a very "old-school-kind-of-way"; no workshops in groups, almost no powerpoints, just the professors explaining the theories and us, students, taking notes non-stop.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Everything worked out in a very "old-school-kind-of-way"; no workshops in groups, almost no powerpoints, just the professors explaining the theories and us, students, taking notes non-stop.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: Sports club... Never tried it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go hang out at the cafés, at the restaurants, at the museums, in the gardens, in the public libraries.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Maybe take the train to Normandie, Lyon or Marseille.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. (i'm half french).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be polite and say yes to almost everything.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think that it is super important for the Parisians that you are polite in a very "old-school-kind-of-way". Fx, you shud never say the first name of your professors - instead say "Madame/Monsieur + last name", always speak to people with "vous" (unless you are talking with some of your good friends/family), always say "merci beaucoup" for everything, and apologies if you did anything wrong or misunderstood something.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the late-night-dinning. A lot of the Parisians work very hard all the time, but no matter what they always find the time to go out with the ones they love. "the streets of Paris is their livingroom".

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Unless your french is super good; do not go there. 
Or take a lot of french classes before your arrival. 

If your french is super good; be polite, reach out to the administration of UCPH, and try your best to get some friends who have lived in Paris for a long time, so they can help you, if you get into trouble.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep calm - and reach out to someone like me at our Facebook group (for the students of UCPG), we will try our best to help you!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I found some really good friends, and now I feel like Paris is my second home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not to panic.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
